pages.title: Sharing Images in Chat
pages.text: While the chat screen is open, drag one or more image files into the game window. Each image appears inline in the chat and is synced to all online players.$(br2)Multiple files can be dropped at once — each image is sent as a separate chat message.

pages.title: How to Use
pages.text: $(bold)1.$() Press the chat key (default $(key)T$() or $(key)/$(key)) to open the chat screen.$(br2)$(bold)2.$() Keep the chat screen open and drag one or more image files into the game window.$(br2)$(bold)3.$() Release — the images appear in chat immediately and are synced to other players.

pages.title: How Images are Rendered
pages.text: Chat images are injected via a Mixin into the vanilla ChatComponent render method. When rendering a chat line, DragIt checks if the message starts with the $(bold)!image:$() prefix. If so, it parses the remainder as a ResourceLocation and renders the image in-place.$(br2)Images are scaled proportionally to fit within the configured maximum $(bold)width and height$() limits.

pages.title: Hover to Enlarge
pages.text: Hovering your mouse over a chat image $(bold)enlarges it$() to the center of the screen, scaled to the maximum size that fits within the current GUI dimensions.$(br2)Moving the mouse away returns the image to its normal chat size.

pages.title: Blank Line Padding
pages.text: Because Minecraft chat lines are each 9 pixels tall, an image taller than one line would overlap with subsequent messages. DragIt calculates how many chat lines the rendered image occupies and automatically inserts that many blank lines after the image to prevent overlap.

pages.title: Notes
pages.text: • Chat images are $(bold)not persisted$() — they disappear after leaving the server$(br)• All chat image textures are released when you disconnect$(br)• Images are compressed before sending using the smaller of the server-side and client-side pixel limits$(br2)$(note)If your UUID is on the server blacklist (or not on the whitelist when "All" is false), images will only be visible to you locally.$()
